title: Building and checking RAG
goal: Connect retrieved evidence to an answer and abstain when support is absent.
case: The college-policy assistant answers questions with policy IDs.
terms: Retrieve relevant text for the current request, then draft an answer bounded by that text.
Check every material claim against the cited passage.
If approved sources lack an answer, return a clear unsupported status.
Use 20 practice questions for improvements and keep ten separate questions for final checking.
steps: Produce an extractive classroom answer with a source ID
Compare top-1 and top-2 on practice cases
example: P3: Students may request one deadline extension within seven days.
Q: How many extensions are allowed?
misconception: A citation label proves that the cited passage supports the answer.
correction: Read the passage and check that it entails the claim; a plausible-looking source tag can be wrong.
change: Replace a relevant passage with an irrelevant one and observe abstention.
metric: Supported claims / checked claims and no-answer accuracy
lab: Run a small extractive retrieval and answer pipeline.
output: Twenty-case practice table; ten final questions remain sealed for assessment.
